title: Ask an Imam or Teacher Well
whyMatters: Good questions often receive better answers. Learning how to ask an imam or qualified teacher helps you avoid confusion, get relevant guidance, and know when a matter needs personal review.

subSteps: State what happened, what decision you need to make, and where you live.
Mention deadlines, family pressure, health issues, or financial details if they matter.
Leave out private details that do not affect the question.
Say that you are a new Muslim and need the practical next step.
Ask what must be done now and what can wait.
Ask whether there are differences of opinion you should know about without deep details.

exactActions.text: Check the answer before acting on sensitive matters
subSteps: Marriage, divorce, inheritance, zakat, abuse, medical issues, and legal concerns need careful review.
Do not rely on anonymous comments for major life decisions.
Seek professional help where the issue is medical, legal, or financial.

timeEstimate: 10-20 minutes to prepare a clear question

obstacles.problem: I feel embarrassed asking basic questions
obstacles.solution: Basic questions are exactly what teachers expect from beginners. Clear humility is better than silent confusion.
Ask the teacher to explain what applies to your situation and what can wait. If needed, ask a qualified local scholar who knows your context.

tinyVersion: Write: what happened, what you need to decide, and that you are a new Muslim.
unlocksNext: Good questions help you keep learning with confidence and avoid acting on unreliable advice.

gentleScripts.title: Asking for a beginner answer
gentleScripts.body: I am a new Muslim and I am trying to do this correctly without becoming overwhelmed. What is the practical next step for my situation, and what can wait?
